canonical_concept.beeja: ऐं (Aim) — the bīja of Sarasvatī, the Goddess of knowledge. Aim is the bīja of vidyā in all its forms.
canonical_concept.vyakarana: Vidyā is a feminine noun derived from the root vid (to know) with the suffix -yā. The feminine gender reflects the Indian tradition of treating knowledge as the Goddess (Sarasvatī).
canonical_concept.functional_meaning: Vidyā is the knowledge that liberates. The Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad distinguishes two types of vidyā: Parā Vidyā (higher knowledge — knowledge of Brahman that leads to liberation) and Aparā Vidyā (lower knowledge — the fourteen traditional sciences including the Vedas, Vedāṅgas, and other disciplines). True vidyā is not mere information but transformative knowledge that changes the knower.
canonical_concept.dhatu: विद् (Vid) — To know, to find, to exist. The root vid is one of the most productive roots in Sanskrit — it gives vidyā (knowledge), veda (that which is known), vedana (sensation), vidvān (the knower).
canonical_concept.nirukta: "Vidyate anayā iti vidyā" — that by which one knows. Also: "vindati iti vidyā" — that which is found/discovered. Knowledge is not created but discovered — it already exists and is revealed through study and practice.
related_concepts: samskara (vidyārambha — the saṃskāra of beginning education)
canonical_concept.tattva: Vidyā-Tattva — the principle of knowledge and illumination. In Advaita: Vidyā (knowledge) is the direct means of liberation — it removes avidyā (ignorance). In Kashmir Śaivism: Vidyā is one of the thirty-six tattvas — the principle of limited knowledge that characterizes the bound soul.

claims.value: In Advaita Vedānta: Vidyā (knowledge of Brahman) is the direct means of liberation — it removes avidyā (ignorance) which is the cause of bondage. In Mīmāṃsā: Vidyā is the knowledge of Vedic injunctions — the means of achieving dharmic results. In Nyāya: Vidyā is valid knowledge (pramā) obtained through the four pramāṇas (perception, inference, comparison, testimony).

provenance.source_text: Sarasvatī Vandanā (traditional prayer to the Goddess of knowledge)

claims.value: In Vedic cosmology: Vidyā is the cosmic knowledge that Brahma used to create the universe. The concept of Brahma-vidyā (knowledge of Brahman) as the cosmic principle of self-knowledge. The Purāṇas describe Sarasvatī as the Goddess of all vidyā — she dwells on the tongue of the learned.

provenance.source_text: Sarasvatī Vandanā (traditional prayer to the Goddess of knowledge)

claims.value: Vidyā as psychological transformation: true knowledge (vidyā) transforms the knower — it is not merely intellectual but experiential. The concept of jñāna-yoga (the yoga of knowledge) as the path of vidyā. The psychology of vidyā: it removes the three psychological obstacles — āvaraṇa (concealment), vikṣepa (distraction), and mala (impurity).

provenance.source_text: Sarasvatī Vandanā (traditional prayer to the Goddess of knowledge)

claims.value: The concept of vidyā in governance: the Arthaśāstra prescribes the fourteen vidyās for the education of the prince. The concept of rāja-vidyā (royal knowledge) — the Bhagavad Gītā (9.2) calls the knowledge of Brahman "rāja-vidyā" (the king of all knowledge). The educated ruler (vidvān-rājā) is the ideal of Indian political philosophy.

provenance.source_text: Sarasvatī Vandanā (traditional prayer to the Goddess of knowledge)

claims.value: In Āyurveda: Āyurveda itself is a vidyā — the science of life. The concept of āyur-vidyā (the science of longevity). The Caraka Saṃhitā describes the physician's vidyā as encompassing not just medical knowledge but philosophical and ethical knowledge.

provenance.source_text: Sarasvatī Vandanā (traditional prayer to the Goddess of knowledge)

claims.value: The concept of vidyā in mathematics: Gaṇita-vidyā (the science of mathematics) is one of the fourteen traditional vidyās. The concept of vidyā as the discovery of mathematical truth — mathematical knowledge is not invented but discovered (vidyate — it is found).

provenance.source_text: Sarasvatī Vandanā (traditional prayer to the Goddess of knowledge)

claims.value: In Jyotiṣa: Jyotiṣa-vidyā (the science of light/astronomy) is one of the six Vedāṅgas. The concept of vidyā in astronomy: the knowledge of celestial patterns that reveals the cosmic order.

provenance.source_text: Sarasvatī Vandanā (traditional prayer to the Goddess of knowledge)

claims.value: In alchemical traditions: Rasaśāstra is a vidyā — the science of mercury and metals. The concept of dhātu-vidyā (the science of metals) as a sacred knowledge transmitted through the Guru-śiṣya relationship.

provenance.source_text: Sarasvatī Vandanā (traditional prayer to the Goddess of knowledge)

claims.value: The Vidyārambha saṃskāra (beginning of education) is the ritual initiation into vidyā. The Upanayana saṃskāra initiates the student into the study of the Vedas — the highest vidyā. The concept of vidyā-dāna (gift of knowledge) as the highest form of charity.

provenance.source_text: Sarasvatī Vandanā (traditional prayer to the Goddess of knowledge)

claims.value: The lamp (dīpa) symbolizes vidyā — knowledge illuminates the darkness of ignorance. The book (pustaka) symbolizes vidyā. The lotus symbolizes vidyā — pure knowledge blooming from the waters of the mind. Sarasvatī's vīṇā (lute) symbolizes the harmony of vidyā.
